content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
Your summary has no dates or durations, so I can't state or calculate years of experience. **How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** If you can't give a single number, the start and end dates of each role would let me calculate it.

**What it costs to leave it out:**

- **Failing the screen on the one hard requirement.** The posting names exactly one requirement, "8 years of backend engineering experience." Recruiters and applicant-tracking systems often check for it directly. A summary with no number can be filtered out before anyone reads your project work.
- **Being read as junior.** Readers tend to assume missing years means fewer years than required, not more.
- **Unused strengths.** The 40,000-orders-a-day pipeline is solid evidence, but it shows scale, not tenure. Without a stated duration it can't satisfy the requirement.

I won't make up a figure, because an unsupported number could fall apart at the interview or background-check stage.

**Draft ready for your number:**

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Previous work includes payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

If X is 8 or more, this meets the requirement as written. If it's under 8, tell me the actual figure and I'll rework the summary to emphasize scale and domain depth.
